Replace.Text: Allows stacking up to two combat units per tile. Plots that allow for a garrison (Cities, Forts and Citadels) will be able to stack up to three combat units.
Disables Research Agreements with other civilizations.
The human player will always get the best starting location on any given map. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The start bias of your chosen civilization will be ignored when this option is selected.
Citadels can be built in, and claim tiles from, the territory of another Civilization or City-State only if you are at war with it. Otherwise they claim only tiles in neutral territory.
Each era's technologies cost more than the last: +10% per era, starting in the Ancient Era, up to 1.8 times in the Information Era. A longer game puts more units on the map, which uses more memory.

AI civilizations will not send Missionaries or Great Prophets to cities owned by a human player who has founded a religion of their own.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Humans without a religion remain valid targets -- the protection only applies once you have a religion to defend.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Note: passive religion pressure from neighbouring foreign cities is unaffected.
AI players are only ever allowed to build or own one city.
Blocks the AI from building [COLOR_WATER_TEXT]World Wonders[ENDCOLOR].
Removes combat damage randomness so it's always 100% damage (instead of in a range between 80% damage and 120% damage).
Removes the XP Caps from:[NEWLINE]Forts, Citadels, other improvements and city garrisons, Barbarians and City-States.

Only Recon units (Scouts, Explorers and their successors) can claim Ancient Ruins. Any other unit that steps onto a ruin leaves it intact for a Recon unit to claim later. City border growth still claims ruins normally.
Ancient ruin rewards that would grant a free Technology instead grant a lump of Science, banked into your current research.

Fog of War creeps back over explored land you can no longer see, so the map must be re-scouted. Cities and their surroundings, your own territory, natural wonders, mountains, ancient ruins, and fully-explored continents stay revealed. Applies to all players.

During war, your combat land units capture the enemy tiles they occupy and eligible neighbouring ones. Forts and citadels can only be taken by occupying them; taking a citadel also claims the tiles around it. Conquered tiles are returned when you make peace.

Embarked land units cannot enter Ocean tiles: armies and settlers cross the Ocean aboard a Troop Transport, or one unit at a time in the troop berth of a melee warship from the Renaissance on.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The rule binds human players only. The AI still sails its naval invasions and overseas settlers in escorted Troop Transports whenever it can get them; it is exempt only so that edge cases (no ship ready in time, or a move no transport covers) never leave it stranded, which would be overly harsh.

Once per turn, when you and a met, visible rival are both building the same World Wonder, you are told whether you are ahead or behind and by how many turns. Fog-of-war honest: only rivals whose city you can currently see are counted.

Allows you to make rival civilizations your vassal state. A civilization capitulates in a peace treaty only if you hold its original capital; liberating a civilization's original capital makes it your voluntary vassal.
The Vassal Overview opens once you reach the Medieval Era or become another civilization's vassal.

Once the conditions below are met, your vassal may ask you for independence at any time. Refusing means war with them. An AI vassal is more likely to ask when they feel mistreated or believe they could win that war.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Your vassal may seek independence once the following are true:

Once the conditions below are met, you may ask your master for independence at any time. If they refuse, they will declare war on you. An AI master is more likely to agree if they like you or fear your military.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]You may seek independence once the following are true:
1. At least {1_NumTurns} turns as a vassal
